extracted.intended_audience: researchers, donors, patients, and stakeholders interested in Lustgarten Foundation pancreatic cancer funding
extracted.subtask_description: A public portfolio page listing grants funded by the Lustgarten Foundation across multiple programs (LABS, Clinical Research, Focused Research, Career Development, Innovation & Collaboration, Partnerships). Shows project titles, PIs, institutions, start/end dates, and grant amounts — useful for understanding funding priorities and examples of supported work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational mission — transformative pancreatic cancer research
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing the Best Science to Transform Pancreatic Cancer into a Curable Disease. 'We are committed to ushering in a new era in pancreatic cancer research, accelerating progress and improving survival so everyone impacted by pancreatic cancer can experience more hope for the future, more time with their loved ones, and less fear.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation emphasizes work that can change, extend, and save patients' lives; proposals should articulate translational impact on survival, patient outcomes, or pathways to a cure. Funded projects on the page illustrate this focus (early detection, immunotherapy, precision therapy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority on boldness and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation states a 'relentless focus on funding the boldest, most innovative studies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for high-risk/high-reward proposals and novel approaches is implied. Examples of funded projects include cutting-edge immunotherapies, AI-augmented early detection, and novel targeted therapies, indicating innovation across basic, translational, and clinical domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: LABS Program
rubrics_metrics.description: A Translational Convergence Program and Dedicated Laboratory awards (e.g., multiple $5,000,000 awards to established labs at Johns Hopkins, MIT, CSHL, Salk) supporting long-term, large-scale laboratory initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These awards are multi-year, multi-million-dollar investments supporting dedicated labs focused on priorities like early detection, cancer genetics, targeted immunotherapy, and precision detection/therapy. Ideal applicants are high-capacity labs with leadership and institutional support capable of sustained, translational research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Research funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for clinical trials and clinical-translational studies, including multi-institutional consortia, window-of-opportunity trials, pilot studies, and combinatorial therapy trials (examples: PASS-02 consortium, neoadjuvant hepatic artery chemotherapy trials, combinatorial myeloid activation immunotherapy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation funds interventional and translational clinical studies with clear clinical endpoints or feasibility for changing practice; it also supports trial infrastructure, recruitment strategies, and diversity initiatives. Grants in this category range from mid-six figures to low millions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused Research Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller directed awards for specific mechanistic, technological, or preclinical projects (examples include mechanisms of innervation, macrophage roles in metastasis, AI-augmented early detection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grants typically fund targeted, often shorter-term projects (amounts shown around $100k–$500k). They are suitable for discrete studies that address well-defined hypotheses or develop/validate new techniques relevant to pancreatic cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards supporting early-career investigators (examples: $300,000 awards for projects on metabolic adaptations, KRAS inhibitor resistance, autophagy inhibition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to support rising investigators to develop independent research programs relevant to pancreatic cancer. Typical award size and duration are indicated by the listed grants (~$300k across multiple years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation & Collaboration awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller awards aimed at fostering innovative ideas and collaborative efforts (examples: $110,000 grants for tumor-stromal network projects, choline transport vulnerability studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These awards appear intended to catalyze early-stage collaborative work or pilot studies that could scale to larger projects if successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for partnered projects and external collaborations (examples include international and institutional partners; Partnership-listed grants ~$300,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation funds collaborative and partnership-based projects, including those extending across institutions and geographies, to leverage complementary expertise and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding scale and duration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant amounts on the page range from approximately $110,000 to $5,000,000 with project durations from ~1 year up to 5 years (projected start/end dates provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can infer expected budget and timeframe envelopes by program: LABS and Dedicated Laboratory awards are multi‑million and multi‑year; Clinical and Focused grants vary from mid-six-figures to millions; Career Development and Innovation grants are mid- to low-six-figure awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic research priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurring themes among funded projects include: early detection and diagnostics, immunotherapy and tumor immunology, precision/targeted therapy, AI and computational approaches for detection/management, tumor microenvironment/stroma, organoids/personalized therapeutics, and mechanisms of metastasis and therapy resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals aligning with these thematic areas have strong representation among funded awards and thus may align well with Foundation priorities; page examples provide concrete project titles and approaches in these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on clinical trial diversity and patient-centered recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded projects include initiatives addressing clinical trial diversity and recruitment barriers (examples: 'IMPACT Diversity', 'Navigated Pancreatic Cancer Multidisciplinary Care to Address Cultural and Language Barriers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation supports efforts to increase enrollment of underserved and non-English-speaking populations and projects that include strategies to improve trial accrual and representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for translational/convergence research
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple program names and project descriptions highlight translational and convergence approaches (e.g., 'Translational Convergence Program', 'Bench to bedside', clinically oriented trials paired with mechanistic studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that link basic/mechanistic discovery to clinical application — bridging laboratory findings to trials or diagnostic implementation — align with the Foundation's stated mission and funded examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated institutional capacity and established leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Many funded awards are to prominent institutions and well-known investigators (Johns Hopkins, Dana‑Farber, MIT, Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, Salk, etc.), and some are named 'Dedicated Laboratory' awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not an explicit eligibility rule on the page, the portfolio suggests a practical preference or likelihood of funding for investigators with substantial institutional support, infrastructure, and track record appropriate to the scale of the requested award.
